summary: 100-ft steel tower in Allendale County, SC (NHLR US 989); register dates it to circa 1935 and calls it a likely Bethlehem Steel model in poor condition.

facts.design: 100-foot steel tower with a 7'x7'x10' steel cab; register says it appears to be a Bethlehem Steel model
facts.agency: Benny Crim, named as administrator on the NHLR page

events.note: Register says built circa 1935; builder not named
Registered March 27, 2014; nominated by Michael T. Finch, Jr.

evidence.supports: tower is in Allendale County and listed as US 989, SC 26
7 by 7 by 10 foot steel cab; appears to be a Bethlehem Steel model
evidence.quote: It features a 7'x7'x10' steel cab and appears to be a Bethlehem Steel model.

evidence.supports: still in original location; poor condition
evidence.quote: Still located in its original location, the tower currently appears to be in poor condition.

evidence.supports: nominated by Michael T. Finch, Jr.
first Forestry Commission fire tower erected in 1930
evidence.quote: The first Forestry Commission fire tower was erected in August, 1930 near Camden.

evidence.supports: two towers each took a bearing on smoke with an alidade
evidence.quote: When a smoke was spotted, each of two towers would record its direction using a large compass table and a sighting device called an alidade.

evidence.supports: fire placed where readings crossed on a map
evidence.quote: The fire was located at the spot where these readings crossed when plotted on a map.

evidence.supports: Commission built about 140 towers between mid-1930s and 1993 (Leesville entry)
evidence.quote: This is one of the original ~140 fire towers built by the South Carolina Forestry Commission between the mid-1930s and the abandonment of the system in 1993.

notes_for_editor: Only one page is about this tower: the NHLR detail page, read in full. Everything tower-specific rests on it. Wikipedia's Ulmer town article has no tower mention. Read for context: the SCFC pictures page and history page, and the NHLR Leesville entry. Not read: the anyplaceamerica topo page and the rootsandrecall Ulmer page. Three search calls ran (one general query, two Ulmer-specific), one over the per-tower budget. Height 100 ft converted to 30.5 m. 'Built circa 1935' is the register's own estimate. The agency field holds the administrator the register names, a person, not an agency. No corrections proposed. Access is unknown: no source gives visiting rules. The photo credit 'Michael T. Finch, Jr.' on the NHLR page was not added as a photo because no license is shown.
